messages:
ameya_international: Hi folks 1 I'm an international hire starting next month. A few quick logistics Qs: do I still need to do an I-9 in person if I have an H-1B and my work authorization is stamped? Also how do we handle direct deposit since my bank is still in my home country for the first two pay cycles? Finally, will benefits cover international remote workers or is there a waiting period?

zoe_peopleops: Welcome Ameya! :wave: Short answers: 1) I-9 still required for all US-based payroll hires. If you're physically in the US on your start date and have H-1B stamped, bring passport + I-94 + I-797 (or current approval notice) to Security for Section 2 verification. If you are remote outside the US at start, we need an authorized agent for Section 2 or you can do an in-person verification the first day you're in a US office.

ameya_international: Thanks. I'll be flying into the Bay Area a few days before start to get visa stamping sorted. Do I need to show the I-94/visa stamp too?

zoe_peopleops: Yes please bring the passport with visa stamp and the most recent I-94 record. I-797 is helpful if you have it. Security will capture those docs and sign the I-9 Section 2. We'll hold a temporary badge until IT hands over laptop.

raj_it: FYI IT will need a US phone number for MFA provisioning. If you don't have one yet, we can provision using a manager-issued loaner number for enrollment and switch to your personal number later. Laptop provisioning scheduled for your first day.

ameya_international: For payroll, my US bank account won't be open until the third week. Can payroll wire to my foreign account for the first pay? Any tax implications?

tax_finance: We can arrange a one-time international wire for the first pay only, but you must complete the cross-border payment form and attach bank SWIFT details. Note: foreign account payments may incur withholding differences and FX fees. Also update your payroll residency in Workday once your US address is active; state withholding will apply from that payroll onward. We'll coordinate a retro tax adjustment if necessary.

ameya_international: Got it. Where do I upload the payroll and visa docs?

zoe_peopleops: Upload all ID/visa docs to Workday HR Docs > Onboarding > Supporting Documents. For the cross-border wire, I'll DM the payment form pdf. For direct deposit, once you open a US account, add it in Workday > Pay > Bank Accounts; payroll cutoffs are on the 25th each month.

hr_bot: Background check for ameya_international: INITIATED 1 consent received. International reference checks may take longer 1 estimated completion 7-10 business days. Ref: BG-9451.

ameya_international: One more: benefits eligibility while Im remote overseas for the first 2 weeks? I plan to be on US soil by day 1 but will travel back briefly.

zoe_peopleops: Benefits enrollment opens on your first US calendar day on payroll and you have 30 days to elect. Medical plans require US primary care coverage; if you are outside the US during the effective date, coverage may be delayed until you're back in-country. We'll flag your case for benefits team to confirm effective date.

security_bot: Note for Security: will perform I-9 Section 2 on arrival 8:30am (Ameya). Temporary visitor badge issued until HR completes verification. Please keep package at reception for laptop pickup.

ameya_international: Thank you all 1 really helpful. Last small ask: is there a relocation/travel advance for visa stamping costs?

zoe_peopleops: We have a relocation travel policy for eligible new hires. If your manager approved visa-stamp travel as part of your offer, submit receipts in Concur under "Relocation" within 30 days. If not, send a quick note here and we'll route an exception to people-ops and finance.

raj_it: Ping me the morning of your arrival and I'll meet you at Security to help with laptop and MFA setup.

ameya_international: Will do 1 thanks everyone :grinning:
